The Diploma of Business is an 8-unit course over two or three trimesters, designed as a pathway to a Bachelor of Business degree for domestic and international students. It provides an AQF Level 5 qualification, aiding students in launching careers in various business areas or enhancing employability for advancement.

This course suits students who:

  • lack the results for entry into the Bachelor of Business degree
  • want to start a career with a nationally recognized qualification
  • seek to improve employability for career advancement.
6vd5:
The Diploma of Information Technology is an 8-unit course over two or three trimesters, designed as a pathway to a Bachelor of Information Technology (Business Information Systems) degree for both domestic and international students. It provides an AQF Level 5 qualification, enabling students to confidently start careers in various IT fields or enhance their employability for advancement.

This course is suitable for students who:

  • lack the results for entry into a Bachelor of Information Technology degree
  • want to start a career in IT with a nationally recognized qualification
  • seek to improve employability for career advancement

This Postgraduate Qualifying Program is a 5-unit course delivered over one trimester. It has been specifically designed as a pathway to a master’s degree for international students who do not meet the entry requirements for a master’s program.

This course is suitable for individuals who:

  • do not possess the requisite qualifications to gain entry into their desired master’s degree
  • require adaptation to the academic standards expected in master’s degree studies
  • seek additional support in English language proficiency

Upon successful completion of this program, students will be well-prepared to commence their postgraduate degree studies with confidence at Murdoch University.

Master of Community Development (M1212) (081029E)

This course will introduce students to the concepts and practices of community development utilized to create and promote community-led change in various settings across Australia and beyond. It is designed for community work practitioners and graduates who are interested in transitioning into emerging fields that embrace community development principles and wish to significantly expand their knowledge through further postgraduate studies.

Master of Criminology (M1314) (103447A)

This course will equip students with the skills necessary to comprehend the fundamental aspects of criminology. Regardless of whether students have graduated with a degree in criminology or from another discipline, they will acquire in-depth knowledge and skills to analyze contemporary issues facing today’s criminal justice system. Additionally, this course offers the option to complete a thesis, providing students the opportunity to specialize in an area of criminology they are passionate about while demonstrating their readiness for PhD studies.

Master of Development Studies (M1195) (077165J)

Students will explore the interconnections between politics, governance, and development, as well as social and environmental sustainability, food and health security, gender empowerment, and state building and conflict. Additionally, they will evaluate various approaches to policy and practice. Graduates will acquire the skills and knowledge necessary to pursue a career in international development across a diverse range of settings, including regional and international organizations, government agencies, consultancy firms, and non-governmental organizations (NGOs) engaged in development initiatives.
